newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Getronics sees boost from euro, 2000.
newsitem.headline: Getronics sees boost from euro, 2000.

text.p: Dutch electronics firm Getronics NV said on Friday that systems changes forced by the millennium and the advent of the single European currency could boost its turnover by around 500 million guilders.

Chairman Ton Risseeuw told Reuters the company eyed about five percent of the estimated 10 billion guilders extra turnover in the Dutch market coming from changes that systems and program operators would have to make by 1999 and 2000.
"We expect to get about five percent of this market which we have estimated at 10 billion guilders," he said.
Getronics had 1996 turnover of 2.21 billion guilders.
Risseeuw said he expected "explosive" growth in demand from customers facing problems ahead of the introduction of the euro and the arrival of the millennium.
But he forecast a fall-off after 1998 by which time new systems would have to be in place to cope with the changes.
Risseeuw warned that many firms have been slow to address the likely problems caused by the double change.
Getronics earlier posted 35 percent higher 1996 net profit of 132 million guilders and Risseeuw said the firm could achieve 20 percent annual earnings per share growth in the years ahead.
EPS rose over 33 percent in 1996 to 1.52 guilders per share.
